newsitem.title: PERU: Shougang Peru, Korea's Hyundai mull $300 mln deal.
newsitem.headline: Shougang Peru, Korea's Hyundai mull $300 mln deal.

text.p: Peru's only iron producer, Shougang Hierro Peru, said Monday it has signed a letter of intent with South Korea's Hyundai Corp. to build a 300 megawatt (MW) electricity plant costing $300 million.

"We have signed a letter of intent to analyze a 300 MW coal-driven electricity plant," general manager Raul Vera La Torre said. Shougang Corp, China's state iron company, bought Peru's state-run Hierro Peru S.A. and its facilities at Marcona, 250 miles south (400 km) of Lima, in November 1992 for $120 million.

Under the terms of the sale, Shougang has also committed itself to a timetable worked out with Peru's privatization board to invest $10 million this year, $27 million in 1997 and $100 million in the following two years.

Shougang's production in the first seven months of the year fell 19.9 percent to 1.932 million tonnes, compared with the same period last year, according to latest Energy and Mines Ministry figures. Last year, output dropped 14.33 percent drop last year to 3.897 million tons compared with 4.549 million tons in 1994.
Last week Hyundai announced plans to invest $1.3 billion in Peru, especially in the mining sector.
